title: Urgent vs Non-Urgent Priority Task Queue
problemStatement: Implement `createPriorityScheduler()` that queues tasks labeled `'urgent'` (Priority 1) and `'transition'` (Priority 2). `flush()` must ALWAYS execute all urgent tasks before executing any transition tasks.
interviewTrap: In React 18's Lane model, urgent events (keystrokes) interrupt running transition fibers, discarding in-progress work to preserve 60fps input responsiveness.

testCases.name: Executes urgent tasks before older transition tasks
testCases.testFn: const s = createPriorityScheduler(); s.schedule(() => 'transition-1', 'transition'); s.schedule(() => 'urgent-1', 'urgent'); return s.flush();

testCases.name: Maintains FIFO order within same priority level
testCases.input: multiple urgent tasks execute in insertion order
testCases.testFn: const s = createPriorityScheduler(); s.schedule(() => 'u1', 'urgent'); s.schedule(() => 't1', 'transition'); s.schedule(() => 'u2', 'urgent'); return s.flush();

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: React categorizes updates into Urgent (typing in an `<input>`, clicks) and Non-Urgent / Transition (filtering a 10,000 item list). Wrapping an update in `startTransition(() => setQuery(text))` allows React to interrupt the list render if the user types another keystroke.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Render Phase: Fiber node evaluation and hooks linked-list dispatch for Lanes / Priority-Based Task Scheduling.
2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.
